Hi Jenna —

Appreciate the clear priorities. I've attached our completed RFI PDF and a short matrix that enumerates retention/obfuscation practices for ephemeral KV/cache material. High-level notes up front:

- Detection & monitoring: We provide both rules-based detectors (customer-configurable) and signal-aggregation ML detectors that flag potential policy violations in real time. We expose alert hooks and a webhook for aggregated incidents.
- Thresholds & tuning: Customers can tune sensitivity per route and set auto-escalation policies; we ship recommended defaults for high-risk domains (finance, healthcare).
- Artifacts & retention: By default, Redwood does not persist full request-response payloads beyond 30 days in hosted mode; KV cache is purged per model session unless explicitly configured for long-term caching by the customer. Private/Dedicated customers can set retention to 0 and retain logs on-prem.
- Incident response SLA: We offer 24x7 triage for P1 incidents with guaranteed 1-hour response for Dedicated customers; hosted customers receive prioritized support with 4-hour initial response.

Attachments: Redwood_Content_Governance_RFI_20260212.pdf (answers), data_retention_matrix.xlsx

If it's useful, Marcus (legal/commercial) and Karthik (security integrations) are on the thread to confirm SLA language and technical connectors. Happy to walk through the doc on a call next week.

Best,
